utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-42/2-PT, the Prosecutor versus Vladimir Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We're here for a hearing on a request under Rule 11 bis. May I have the appearances. Prosecution, first.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Again, good afternoon, Your Honours, counsel, esteemed members from Serbia. For the Prosecution, Susan Somers. To my right, Mr. David Re, trial attorney; to his right, Ms. Carmela Javier, case manager. Behind me is Mr. Phillip Weiner, trial attorney, and Mr. Aleksandar Kontic, trial attorney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, my learned colleagues and everybody else present in the courtroom, especially the representatives of the state. I am representing Mr. Vladimir Kovacevic, and I'm assisted by Mr. Dragoslav Djukic, my temporary case manager that has been assigned by the registry to me for these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Radosavljevic. The Chamber has invited representatives of the Republic of Serbia. Could you, although it's on record in another case, but could you please introduce yourself. Mr. Obradovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In spite of this, Your Honour, I will wish you a good day again, also to all the others present. My name is Sasa Obradovic. I am the First Advisor at the Embassy of the Republic of Serbia in The Hague, and with me is Mr. Dusan Knezevic, the Deputy Prosecutor for war crimes. Today we shall be representing the Government of Serbia. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Obradovic. This hearing is scheduled to give an opportunity to the parties and to the representatives of Serbia to make additional oral submissions. The Chamber is not seeking any repetition of what is already in your written submissions, but since, when writing these submissions, you do not know what the other party will write or what the other information will be; apart from that there may be new developments. So therefore I would like to give an opportunity to you first, Ms. Somers, to address the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. With the same request that I may not use all my time right now, but I might have an opportunity to respond to anything that should arise in the course of this proceeding. The characterisation of this case would be as a classic 11 bis in what is contemplated by the Security Council. It is an intermediate level or low-level to immediate-level accused, the seniors from which have been before this Tribunal and are under sentence. It is a case which is susceptible of being tried in international jurisdiction with respect to a jurisdiction that is up and running, that has the ability to try cases, as the Chamber has heard from the representatives of Serbia earlier. I just wanted to make sure that it was part of this record as well. The issues that have lingered over the referral have been more in line with the issue of the fluid finding of fitness or not. And just so it is quite clear from our submissions, and I hope it is, that it is our position that it is not a factor in any way barring a referral for the reasons we set forth, but further to emphasise that the Republic of Serbia has responsibly been seized of taking care of this accused for the past two years -- actually, over two years, the affect of the referral would be of really a change in the indictment-seizing tribunal, and there is no limitation that would be evident, either from any logical reading of the Rules or from the actual facts as they exist in this case, which may be more unique than other cases in that provisional release had been granted to the accused prior to even entry of any type of plea, which has not been entered here, which is not required. But the record before the Chamber of Serbia's very active and responsible role is one that we would ask the Court to take great -- to give great weight to, along with, of course, its submissions, which indicate its willingness and ability. And I would defer to any further comment until I have heard any other comment made by my learned colleague opposite. But we wanted to make sure that when the Chamber summarised all of it, it boiled down very much to these essential points. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Somers. Ms. Radosavljevic, I would like to give you an opportunity as well to add anything to what you have already submitted in writing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, as the Defence has already stated in its written submission, the Defence of Mr. Kovacevic accepts the legal submission both of the state and of the Prosecution that refer to the applicability of a case such as this to a national court. What I mean is that the submissions on the gravity of the crime, in light of the other proceedings before the ICTY, is -- in light of the gravity of the crime, Rule 11 bis is applicable in this case. Also, the position of Mr. Kovacevic in the military hierarchy in regards of the crime charged is a mid-level or even maybe a lower-level position, and especially having in mind that his superiors have already been tried in this Tribunal, this case would be applicable for a referral under 11 bis. Also, the legislation of Serbia Montenegro, now only Serbia, in the last few years brought the national law closer to the practice of the ICTY, and that has already been uttered in both the submissions of the state and of the Office of the Prosecution. We, as you already have been informed, have a new law on the protection programme of the participants in criminal proceedings, which was brought in 2005, and also the law on the organisation and jurisdiction of state organs in the proceeding against war crimes, brought in 2003 with changes in 2004 and 2005. Also, I would take the opportunity, just briefly, to state a personal opinion that as a member of the Belgrade bar and of the legal system of my state, I am very glad that the cooperation between my country and the Office of the Prosecution of the International Criminal Tribunal is at this high level. Having in mind that the Referral Chamber has ordered the parties to make oral submission related to the mental health of the accused at the hearing to be scheduled, as it is said, in the order issued on the 17th of July, the Defence would like to take the opportunity and to state again, that, in this particular case, the position of the Defence is that it opposes to a referral of the case. This position is not out of legal reasons but out of factual reasons concerning the particular accused and his circumstances. Mr. Vladimir Kovacevic, the accused, has been transferred to the UN Detention Unit and has been under the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia since the 23rd of October, 2003. From this day up until the present day, the accused underwent seven examinations by medical expert witnesses. In December 2003, he underwent the examination by the medical expert witness team appointed by the Trial Chamber, Dr. Goreta and Professor Krajinovic. After that, in February 2004, he underwent an examination conducted by Dr. Dusan Kosovic, a medical expert witness of the Defence. In December 2004, we had again an examination performed by the -- performed by the Trial Chamber-appointed expert -- medical expert witnesses. Then in March 2005, Dr. Rosic was the examiner. She was a medical expert witness of the Defence. At last, in October 2005, he went through three examinations in a period of three weeks that were medical expert witnesses of the Trial Chamber, Dr. Goreta and Professor Krajinovic. Then Ana Najman and Dr. Vladimir Ortakov which were -- which were the team -- the Defence medical expert witness team. And at last the medical expert team that the Prosecution sent, Dr. Folnegovic and Professor Zakic. So altogether seven examinations. These examinations included a lot of hours of conversation of my client and also of tests that he performed which were very exhausting for him. And at the end the Trial Chamber has reached a decision on 7 April 2006 with which the Trial Chamber declared the accused not fit to plea or not fit to stand trial. This decision was without any prejudice to any further criminal proceedings against Mr. Kovacevic. The Defence would like to refer to some parts, very short parts, of the expert witnesses' reports in this case that will show the Chamber why the Defence opposes a referral under the Rule 11 bis, and therefore I would ask if we could -- because all those reports were submitted confidential, if we could just for five minutes enter into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Registrar, the Chamber would like to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Ms. Radosavljevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Should this case be referred to the national courts -- court at this point, under the national law, it would be necessary to undertake another examination of Mr. Kovacevic. Just to repeat my last sentences from the private session, the opinion thinks -- the Defence is of the opinion that this would just derogate the already poor mental health of Mr. Kovacevic. Another question that is more rhetorically is the following: Should this case be referred to the national court? And the accused would be, again, going through the same procedure through which he was going the last two and a half years. What kind of exercise did the participant of the case of Mr. Kovacevic before the Tribunal perform and undertake? And especially having in mind that we are talking about an accused who is mentally challenged. That is all that the Defence has to submit on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Radosavljevic. I would like to give an opportunity, Mr. Obradovic, to add anything to what is already in your written submissions, and they are extensive. They give us a lot of information, not only about criminal law and criminal procedure, but also information about the Serbian law on extradition procedure which informs us about what are the possibilities to take care of someone who is mentally ill and at such a level that you could not just leave him on his own. But if you'd like to add anything, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. We stand by our submission of the 10th of August, which is quite detailed enough and which was not challenged by other parties in these proceedings. My distinguished colleague, Mr. Knezevic, deputy war crimes prosecutor from Belgrade, stands ready to answer any questions you might have about the referral of this case to Serbia, and also any questions about various procedural issues that may arise in view of the special circumstances of this case. Once again, I would like to thank the Prosecution in this case for agreeing with us on the issue that, due to special circumstances in this case, this case should be referred to the Serbian judiciary. In addition to that, I would like to inform the Chamber that I obtained two additional reports today. These reports are of confidential nature, and I would like to know from you whether you wish me to hand you over these two reports, or would you like me to do that at the Status Conference which follows immediately after this hearing? I'm also prepared to do this in private session, in view of the fact that this concerns confidential information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Obradovic, if these reports would show any significant change in the health condition of Mr. Kovacevic, then the Referral Bench would like to be informed about it. If there is no significant change, then the Referral Bench would be satisfied if it would be dealt with at the Status Conference to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the problem lies in the fact that it is difficult for me to assess whether there are any changes or not. Given that these are confidential reports, you must be aware that I was not privy to previous reports which were also confidential. Also, the additional problem is there was some delay in us receiving this, and I made sure that I had these two reports when coming today -- to today's hearing. So I can't give an answer to your question. At any rate, a copy can be made and we can provide these reports to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest to the parties the following procedure: Since reporting is done before a Trial Chamber, and the Referral Bench only has a global insight and the final conclusions, that the new reports will be presented to the Trial Chamber or the Judge sitting on the Status Conference. If the Trial Chamber or the Judge considers that there is any significant change in the position the Referral Bench should be aware of, that the parties would express this to the Trial Chamber and the Trial Chamber would then take the initiative to make sure that the information finds its way -- finds, in a transparent way, its way to the Referral Bench. Is that agreeable for the parties? Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I just want to make sure, Your Honour, I understand. Will the parties have an opportunity to see the reports, or will it be a reporting by the Chamber back, basically?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, the reporting always is part of the file before the Trial Chamber, so then of course the parties will have an opportunity to compare this report with other reports they received earlier and can form their opinion on whether this would be relevant to be brought to the attention of the Referral Bench. And, of course, the Trial Chamber might proprio motu decide that it is so relevant that it should be brought to the attention of the Referral Bench. Is that agreeable to you, Ms. Somers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's just to avoid duplication --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and -- yes. Ms. Radosavljevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber will then revisit the matter later today.

utterances.speaker: MR. OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is quite clear, Your Honour. In this case, I suggest that Mr. Knezevic address you about various procedural issues that may arise should this case be referred to Serbia, bearing in mind that there are special circumstances in this case relating to the health condition of the accused, Mr. Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're invited to do so, Mr. Knezevic. At the same time, be aware that the Referral Bench has, of course, read the written submissions in which it's clearly explained how proceedings are -- how they are suspended, when they are resumed. Of course this answers the question the Bench had put to you. And that the Referral Bench has also read the proceedings without consent accommodated in a psychiatric institution, and how those with consent are accommodated in psychiatric institutions, and what the procedures are. So there's no need for repetition, but if you would like to add anything, you can do that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I learned my lesson during the last hearing when I started telling you about what was already contained in our written submissions, so I will do my best not to repeat that mistake now. What I would like to say is: Should this case be referred to a domestic judiciary, what would be the procedural consequences? There are two situations, two possible scenarios. What I fully agree with when it comes to the arguments of the Defence is that, in the further disposition of this case, it will be necessary under our law to perform yet another examination in order to establish whether Mr. Kovacevic was legally competent at the time when the crime was committed and nowadays. There are two possibilities. Should the expert team, should the team of psychiatrists, establish that at the time when the crime was committed he was not sane and that his condition remains the same to this day, in that case, certain security measures would be handed down which would envisage that he needs to be committed to a closed-type mental institution. If it is, on the other hand, established that at the time of the commission of the crimes he was fully, legally competent and sane but that nowadays he's not fit to stand trial and that this is due to a temporary nature of his impairment, then in that case the proceedings would be stayed and additional periodical reports of psychiatrists would be needed, and, if there are any changes, that the proceedings would be reinstated. That's all I have to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Knezevic, for this information. Then I go back to the Prosecution. Is there any need to add anything to what has been said either by the Defence or by the representatives of Serbia? Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just certain aspects of what was in closed session, which I'll be very careful about alluding to, that in fact, although there was a finding of a status, there was no affirmation of a diagnosis, to the best of my recollection. Just the finding of not fit, and I wanted it -- to the best of my recollection, it did not actually confirm, it just said "finding of non-fitness." Secondly, I want to make sure that the Referral Bench has the benefit of being directed to the record at the fitness hearing before the Trial Chamber, particularly to the very detailed testimony of -- sorry, evidence, of Dr. Folnegovic-Smalc, and Ms. Zakic, Danijela Zakic, a psychologist. My colleague points out at paragraph 49 of the decision should be brought to your attention. Where there was any reference to diagnosis was not -- it was to the UNDU. That was strictly the reference. Another point is that the Referral Bench, as in a body, has the opportunity to review the dynamics of the findings of the various experts who've interviewed -- who've conducted medical examinations on the accused, there has not been a static state, there has been dynamism in the findings. It was not consistently not fit and I just wanted to make sure because it's clearly something that if -- although we believe that it is not a relevant factor, I just want to make clear that there were clear indications that it is a situation that is not constant, and that is reflected in the Trial Chamber's decision where there is a specific reference to, should there be a change in, as there had been, resumption of proceedings. And I know it's a terribly long record, it's terribly complex, but it does bear looking at various, rather well-buried in the report, findings that I think are helpful. Having said that, returning to the point that it's not something that really should be a factor, there are no substantive weights technically affected now. It's a procedural venue or forum hearing. I think the Chamber has been provided with very strong commitment and has seen the strong commitment put into action by the Serbian system. And should there be any further question about the Prosecution's reaction, we simply support the decision taken by our respective colleagues from the Republic of Serbia, that they are able to handle it quite adequately, and that the Bench has its mechanism for reporting back, should there be any question about conditions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Somers. Ms. Radosavljevic, anything to add?

utterances.speaker: MS. RADOSAVLJEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. In regards to paragraph 49 and the exact diagnosis of the illness of Mr. Kovacevic, I would like to address the Trial Chamber to look at the transcript of the hearing that was held with all these experts together with the treating doctor of Mr. Kovacevic. This transcript will show that four experts and his treating doctor gave exactly the diagnosis that I cited in the private session, and the two experts of the Prosecution cited another one. As far as the submission of the Prosecution goes towards the possibility of a case that is referred to a national court, can be monitored and then brought back to the Tribunal, I think I don't have to stay that if -- if, in this case, the damage is done, and by "damage is done" I mean the health of my client is even more deteriorating, I don't see that there could be any mechanism that could bring him back to the previous stage. Further on, as far as the submission of the Prosecution goes that his state is a fluid one, I would like to set the attention of the Referral Bench - and I won't quote now, I will just leave it for a later state - to the transcript of the 15 March 2004, pages -- from page 231 to page 237. You will see that there is something that should be addressed when we are talking about the fluid condition of the accused, and that refers to the potential of him being better or not being better in the future. I thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Radosavljevic. May I take it that the representatives of Serbia have nothing to add to this, which is a bit outside the scope of -- perhaps of what -- of the information we specifically asked from you? Is that a correct understanding? Yes? I see you nodding.

utterances.speaker: MR. OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's absolutely correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me ask whether any of my colleague Judges have any questions. Judge Parker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would like to ask, perhaps, Mr. Knezevic two questions: First, one of the positions you suggested could arise if the accused were referred to Serbia is that on examination now or in Serbia, it would be found that while he was of sound mind at the time of the offence, he was temporarily not fit to stand trial at the present. In that situation, what type of medical facilities would be provided? What sort of hospital would he be cared for? And would it be possible for him to continue in the Belgrade military hospital where he's been treated for some time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is what the situation is like: Should his mental health condition be temporary, the trial proceedings would be stayed for a certain period of time. Medical teams or, rather, medical experts would be periodically reporting on his state of health, should his health deteriorate, of course -- or should his health improve, that would be -- the trial would be renewed, proceedings would be reinstated. As for the VMA, that particular institution is open to civilians to be treated and there would be no obstacle for him to continue to be treated in that institution. As stated in the Republic of Serbia's submission, he would be committed to a psychiatric institution, pursuant to the provisions of the law on non-contentious procedure. These are provisions, Article 35 to 55. There it is stated which persons can be detained there. Of course, under the provisions of the law, should his health condition stay the same, his detention at this particular institution can be prolonged. It is not fixed. If the reports arrive to the effect that his state of mind is very poor, there would follow urgent measures for his full committal to that institution. I hope I have answered your question. If not, please, I am open to any additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I am particularly interested in if he would be going to a different institution if he is thought at the moment to be temporarily not fit to stand trial, as opposed to the position if he is found at the moment to be unlikely to recover.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Under our law, Your Honour, there is no such phrase as "highly" or "less likely." He is either temporarily incompetent or permanently incompetent to stand trial. If he is found to be unfit temporarily, then the proceedings are stayed for a while, as I said; and of course if he is found to be unfit for trial permanently, in that case proceedings are in place to terminate that criminal procedure. In both situations, however, there are no impediments that would make it impossible for him to remain -- to be committed in a closed type medical institution. Such persons are a danger to themselves and to others and remain committed to such institutions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So he would, in either case, move from -- in the present situation, move from the hospital or facility where he is presently being treated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KNEZEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. He would remain in the same hospital, because the hospital is fully qualified and has all the facilities for the treatment of such patients.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since there are no further questions, if the last question would have raised any issue, I'd like to hear from the parties. Not for you, Ms. Somers. Not for you, Ms. Radosavljevic. Then we'll adjourn, and the Referral Bench will deliberate whether it has all the information to give a decision or whether it needs further information. If all we need is there, in due course a decision will be given. Otherwise, the parties will hear from us. We'll stand adjourned sine die.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: sine die at 5.46 p.m. 23 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Rule 11 bis hearing adjourned
